propositions: A mutation removed a guard from a shell script performing real deletion; test execution with an empty path variable caused glob expansion to rm -rf /*, destroying /opt/homebrew and /Applications on a contributor workstation.
mutation_gate.py isolates the source tree but not runtime effects; mutation tools (cargo-mutants, mutmut, StrykerJS, PIT) isolate source but none isolate runtime effects.

Both shard-test-executing subprocesses in execute_shard() — baseline pytest and mutmut run mutant test-run — must be wrapped in an OS-enforced sandbox denying writes outside an explicit allow-list, with enforcement verified by observable file-system denial rather than argv inspection.

The sandbox mechanism (Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap on Linux) must be proven to functionally deny writes outside the allow-list and permit writes inside, including denying rm -rf on protected paths, not merely detected by presence-checking.

HOME environment variable must be set to a non-existent path for both sandboxed subprocesses so adjacent home-directory writes fail loudly, verified by call-site binding tests to the hardened environment.
